ending: Yoresh survives the messenger raid, while the Garuda contains the Naga Genesis disaster in the city centre. Jason's deep-astral ritual breaks the invaders' linked aura advantage, and the messenger command ultimately withdraws. Jason defeats Terra June Castor but refuses to kill her. He removes the astral-king brand and seal that bound her, then grants asylum in his astral realm to Terra, a gold-rank messenger commander, the commander's companion, and other defectors. He helps consenting messengers replace their former ruler's marks without making them his slaves, proving their dependence on astral kings can be broken. One messenger dies when the former astral king withdraws its mark before consent can be given. The intervention alerts that astral king and prompts a council. The defectors disagree over concealment and open revolt. An unknown objective beneath a dangerous natural array, a subterranean city, an astral space, and Builder cultists becomes the next likely mission. Purity's core-cleansing relic, regional worm risks, Melody's condition, and the route back to Earth all remain unresolved.
in_short: Recovering from a near-fatal rescue, Jason Asano leaves Rimaros under a false identity and travels with his team while Amos Pensinata trains his aura control. A messenger trail leads the convoy to Yoresh, where a network of world-taker worms has killed whole settlements. The team destroys a breeding site, rescues prisoners, and turns Jason's cloud construct into a refugee hospital and bunker. A Naga Genesis threat erupts as messengers besiege the city. Jason breaks their linked aura suppression with a deep-astral ritual, exposing himself as an alternative to conventional astral-king rule. After sparing Terra June Castor, he removes her binding mark and shelters messenger defectors, later freeing those who consent without enslaving them. Yoresh survives, but Jason's act alerts an astral king. The defectors reveal a deeper campaign around a dangerous natural array and an unknown buried objective, while the searches for Purity's core-cleansing relic and a path to Earth remain open.

recaps.text: Previously: Jason Asano returned from Earth carrying deep trauma and powers that no longer fit ordinary rank expectations. His soul had become a physical astral realm, and his relationships with great astral forces made him both valuable and dangerous to established powers. Farrah Hurin had been revived and shared an unusual residual bond with him. Jason's allies had helped destroy the Builder's flying city, while the Order of Redeeming Light had transformed captives through forced purification. The aftermath left Melody Jane in Jason's custody and Gibson Amouz in specialised care. Rimaros also carried recent losses, including Vesper Rimaros, and Jason's public power had made him a political problem as well as an adventurer. He still hoped to create a bridge back to Earth, but lacked the messenger astral knowledge needed to complete it.

Jason remains in prolonged recovery after a portal rescue nearly killed him and broadcast his aura across Rimaros. His cloud house has changed with his soul, becoming a stronger refuge that unsettles even experienced allies. The Adventure Society and royal representatives propose a public separation from his team, followed by his return under a discreet auxiliary identity. Jason accepts the outline and begins assembling support personnel who can make the cover credible. Meanwhile, an information broker identifies the man responsible for Jason's forced starseed implantation and links him to the Order of Redeeming Light's portal specialist. When the broker is abducted as bait, Jason's allies recognise the trap and arrive with overwhelming support. They rescue the broker and capture the starseed implanter alive. The captive may know the portal specialist's identity, but Jason has not yet decided how to handle him. Jason's recovery, dangerous Astral Gate use, and unwanted prominence also remain unresolved.

Dawn's real auxiliary plan adds trainers, researchers, and a scout to Jason's proposed cover, while Jason refuses to turn his soul space into a prison for Order captives. A group of adventurers then targets a familiar-binding ritual to challenge him. The ritual is moved to safety, and Jason methodically isolates and captures the hunters without killing them. Their Adventure Society standing is likely ruined. Autumn successfully binds a giant frog-like hydra. At the same time, Jason's group prepares for a royal celebration ball intended to reassure Rimaros's political class. Liara Rimaros warns that rival houses may provoke a duel through lesser allies. Jason enters the event expecting manipulation, while Zara Rimaros discusses the royal family's desire to place a representative in his travelling group. Jason refuses to decide until the proposal is handled openly within the family. The party arrives at the ball prepared for the expected political provocation.

The ballroom provocation becomes a series of real duels. Jason first forces an inexperienced challenger to retreat by insisting that any contest carry genuine consequences. A more credible relative then offers cloud-flask materials and vehicle designs as stakes. Soramir Rimaros reopens an old arena, and Jason selects Rufus, Sophie, and Humphrey to fight beside him. Before the matches conclude, four hired gold-rank core users infiltrate Jason's pagoda and use an illegal device that destroys a large part of the structure. Its defences trap and continually injure them. Farrah confronts Jason over the cruelty of his response and helps him recognise the violent habits he brought back from Earth. In the arena, Sophie, Rufus, and Humphrey win their contests. Jason ends his own duel almost immediately with a precise soul attack, forcing Soramir to intervene. The public display confirms that Jason cannot be handled like an ordinary silver-ranker. He prepares to leave Rimaros rather than accept further royal interference.

Jason transfers the captured pagoda intruders to Liara rather than seeking revenge and arranges a decoy departure. A Shade body remains publicly associated with Soramir while the real Jason leaves under his new identity. The convoy includes Jason's team, Amos Pensinata and his nephew's team, Carlos Quilido's mobile prison-hospital, and several other allies. Their route favours populated regions and neglected contracts over speed. In a southern city, Arabelle Remore explains why Callum is so concerned about Melody Jane. Melody is Sophie's mother. She once concealed her family from the Order of the Reaper, entered the Cult of the Reaper, and was later forced to infiltrate the Order of Redeeming Light. Its purification turned her into an artificial zealot. Jason and Arabelle conclude that Sophie must make decisions for Melody while Melody cannot give informed consent. The revelation transforms Melody from a dangerous prisoner into an unresolved family responsibility.

Carlos continues stabilising Gibson Amouz, whose incomplete purification may offer clues for treating Melody and other converted victims. Amos begins intensive aura training with Jason, demanding precise control rather than raw force. The convoy reaches the ruins of Cartes, where a stolen astral space and a diamond-rank monster left a vast destruction zone. Jason registers as the cook John Miller to preserve his cover. He discovers a hidden Builder cult site and nearly exposes himself through an uncontrolled aura response, but the team presents him only as a sanctioned asset. Their work shows that the damaged region needs logistics more than additional combat teams, so the convoy moves on toward places where its abilities can make a material difference. Belinda's escalating thefts also force Humphrey to warn that her behaviour could endanger the whole team's reputation. The group leaves Cartes with Jason's identity intact, a clearer route, and Corinne Peskos's independent silver-rank team travelling alongside it.

Estella reports possible messenger activity near Yoresh, giving Jason both a threat to pursue and a possible source of astral knowledge for the unfinished Earth bridge. Farrah and Travis leave the convoy for Rimaros to develop long-distance communications and magitek weapons, making Jason's separation from Farrah immediate despite their residual soul bond. Corinne's team returns with Zara Rimaros, now using the adopted name Zara Noreen after abandoning the succession contest. Jason reacts with hostility because Zara once used his presumed death in a false engagement scheme. Arabelle challenges his surveillance and attempts to control Zara, and Jason agrees that Zara may remain under clinical supervision. Jason then enters Yoresh under the name John Miller with Estella. His covert investigation leads from an indebted pub owner to underground fight dens, where he enters a suppression-collar tournament and identifies an outworlder promoter. Taika, meanwhile, nears silver rank and resolves to support Jason without copying his self-destructive pursuit of power.

Jason's arena investigation shifts toward the promoter's elf aide, whose controlled aura suggests a concealed role. Amir Bahadir recognises Jason despite the cover and recruits his team into a worldwide search for a power that may cleanse monster-core effects from souls. Humphrey insists that any decision about such a discovery belongs to the team. The suspected aide is then confirmed as a messenger agent working with Lord Fal. Fal discovers Shade's surveillance and attacks Jason through the familiar link, but the encounter gives the Adventure Society a map of the agent's network. The Society warns that Yoresh's supply lines are vulnerable. Jason's team and Corinne's team are sent south after communications vanish across isolated settlements. The first silent town appears normal from a distance, yet Jason detects abnormal heat loss and identical behaviour among its residents. The teams suspect an externally controlled population positioned close to Yoresh and delay entering until they understand what is governing it.

Carlos identifies a likely heat-consuming parasite. Jason enters the silent settlement and discovers that its residents are corpses controlled by world-taker worms. His anger breaks his concealment, triggering a mass attack. The reunited team uses cold, cleansing, mobility, and wide-area powers to clear thousands of hosts while avoiding direct exposure. Jason and Clive locate a hidden messenger workshop beneath the town. A worm flood overwhelms Jason, but Gordon and Colin prevent the parasites from taking control. The silver-rank messenger operating the facility recognises Jason's body-soul nature and astral power, then becomes terrified of him. Jason defeats her, breaks her will through intimidation, and lets Colin kill and consume her. The wider infestation is confirmed as a deliberate messenger network extending through southern settlements. Although the immediate operator is dead, Jason's conduct troubles both him and his companions. He asks Shade to help keep him from crossing further into cruelty.

The team searches the messenger workshop and frees imprisoned adults, children, and adventurers who had been reserved for experimentation. Neil directs triage, while Sophie, Belinda, Humphrey, Arabelle, and Carlos help stabilise and relocate the survivors. Beneath the prison they find a world-taker worm matriarch and specialised worms. The team destroys the breeding stock rather than risk recreating the weapon. After consuming the matriarch, Colin can begin developing into a Voice of the Will, but doing so would keep the familiar dormant inside Jason's astral realm for an extended period. Jason converts his cloud structure into a hospital and refugee centre as the regional response expands. Disguised elite worm hosts attempt to infiltrate it, but the building traps them. The Healer then appears to Jason and explains that Purity sanctioned himself to create the sought-after core-cleansing relic. The gods will not intervene in the mortal struggle over it. The Healer also gives Jason a one-use core capable of granting true life to an astral construct.

Yoresh prepares for an expected messenger assault. Jason's cloud hospital becomes both a treatment centre for early worm extraction and a heavily defended refugee bunker, though its spirit-domain nature cuts priests off from direct contact with their gods. Inside the city, a messenger collaborator releases a Naga Genesis egg that had been hidden within the soul of the Valash fight promoter. A powerful Garuda hunter allows it to emerge in a form he can fight, and their diamond-rank battle devastates the city centre. Jason's team rescues civilians while Taika reaches silver rank during the evacuation. Messenger forces then surround Yoresh. Their plan is to use summons to thin the adaptive barrier, create temporary breaches, and strike civilian bunkers while the city's strongest defenders are occupied. Jason identifies the bunkers as the true targets. The refugees are sealed into the cloud defences, and the messengers move into position on every side of the city.

The siege begins as messenger summons pour through breaches above the bunkers. Jason's team defends the entertainment district from Onslow's flying shell, while Gareth Xandier leads civilian rescues nearer the centre. Corinne's team uses Zara's hurricane powers to set up large electrical attacks. Humphrey anchors the frontline, Sophie disrupts mobile threats, and Clive and Belinda combine ritual artillery with repeated resets. Jason attempts to spread afflictions through the horde, then shifts to tying down messenger defenders when they contain his chain. The invaders answer the adventurers' momentum with a coordinated aura assault. Jason's pyramid projects his own aura and heavy weapons across the vehicle district. A silver-rank messenger is sent to confront him and is dragged inside, where flight and aura advantages are restricted. Taika intercepts the intruder. His new Garuda authority disrupts the messenger's instincts, beginning a close fight within the shifting cloud corridors as gold-rank messengers prepare to force entry.

Taika defeats the trapped messenger and takes him alive, while the pyramid seals gold-rank intruders away from civilians. Across the entertainment district, messenger aura suppression begins turning the battle. Gordon constructs an alien ritual, and Jason opens his astral gate to power it despite the danger. The resulting projection displays Jason's soul across Yoresh and breaks the harmonic link between messenger auras. Adventurers regain the initiative, while messengers freeze, panic, or become enraged. Their leaders recognise Jason as evidence of an unprecedented route to astral-king power. A diamond-rank messenger moves to kill him, but Wraith intervenes outside normal time and leaves the messenger's corpse at Jason's feet. Jason harvests its life force and gains another resurrection state. Gold-rank enemies still converge on him. Onslow's shell is destroyed, scattering the team, and messenger isolation powers split several members into forced duels as the siege enters its final phase.

Terra June Castor traps Jason in a soul-shell duel that suppresses magic, familiars, items, and outside aid. Their close fight crashes into a civilian bunker. When Terra considers hostages, Jason discovers that his astral realm is inseparable from his soul and can partly resist the suppression. He forces access to Terra's soul, takes control of the duel, and removes both her astral-king brand and the seal holding her at silver rank. Terra survives unconscious. A gold-rank messenger commander then asks Jason for asylum, arguing that only an astral king can shelter the defectors. Jason provisionally accepts and takes the group into his realm. Over the following weeks he helps consenting messengers replace their ruler's marks with their own, refusing to own or coerce them. One dies when the former astral king removes its mark. Yoresh survives and the raid ends in withdrawal. The defectors reveal a deeper campaign around a natural array, a subterranean city, Builder cultists, and an unknown buried objective. Jason expects pressure to lead the next expedition.
